count_answer.interpretation: 50 is the coherent core sequence, including personal introduction, profiles, films, music/radio, archival reading and practical essays. It is not50film plots or50fiction stories. Three dedicated cinema companions are additional; the wider guide also links existing Fakir Mohan and Pratibha profiles. Guide, viewing room, appendices and standalone intro export do not add core chapters.

sequence_integrity.recommendation: Retain core50 and current order; no evidence-driven need for a51st reading merely to grow the count.

reader_journey.assessment: Personal question→literature→writers→stage/radio supplies the purpose before a historical survey. AIR-to-song bridge is concrete and natural.
Music essay followed by contrasting creative lives keeps words and livelihoods connected; Tapu’s choices hand the reader to production rather than ending in a roll of names.

Longest block20readings, but intelligible clusters: Gour/Parbati, performance/colleagues, households/Maya/Nirad, Bhukha/Sabyasachi/Aadim, children/Bir, cross-language/experimental/documentary makers, then collective learning. Do not rearrange chronologically: it would break these paired routes.
Learning→preservation→books forms a useful pause and returns the reader to written sources.
Gourahari/Pratikshya/Anupam and DAMaN/director/editor/producer are distinct process perspectives. Their proximity is purposeful; clarify which Gourahari story became the film.
Two chapters efficiently shift from making to reaching viewers without a separate expansion of the sequence.

Reported commercial performance→resources/obligations→concrete invitations is the correct finish. Futures90–106 returns literature, families, writers/weavers and agreed payment to the reader’s possible next action.

new_user_question.question: Do we need to take five online companion profiles to the book?
new_user_question.recommendation: Do not import all five as full chapters. Add short standalone readings for Bibhuti Pattanaik and Solila Parida; keep Fakir Mohan, Pratibha Ray and Jatindra K. Nayak present through concise integrated portraits and links to their fuller online readings.
new_user_question.count_consequence: If these two additions are accepted, the core becomes 52 readings. Fifty is a useful current count, not a rule that should exclude two distinct contributions. Update hub, contents, chapter references and reading-guide counts together; do not announce 55 chapters merely because five companion pages exist.

profiles.name: Bibhuti Pattanaik
profiles.placement: Part 1, after Kanhu Charan Mohanty and before Manglu Charan Biswal.
profiles.reason: A missing novelist connects books within reach, libraries, editing and book fairs with Badhu Nirupama and a separately credited collaboration on Maya Miriga. That is more than another biography: it makes the author-to-reader infrastructure tangible.
profiles.editorial_scope: Current roughly 315-word narrative is already short. Preserve the distinction between the Badhu Nirupama adaptation and the joint Maya Miriga story credit. Retain the libraries/book-fair opening; avoid expanding the award list.
profiles.overlap: Maya Miriga already names the joint credit (line 30); its link can point to this reading, without adding a second explanation there.

profiles.name: Solila Parida
profiles.form: Short standalone reading, edited from existing profile
profiles.placement: Part 3, after Nandita Das and before Pramod Pati (coordinator-preferred placement, accepted as coherent).
profiles.reason: Adds the producer as an active collaborator: a writer offers a story, a producer gathers people, and script revisions and work across countries carry it towards an audience. This advances the book’s literature-to-making purpose beyond the current short example.
profiles.editorial_scope: Prioritise Pati’s story, Parida’s production role and Kicklighter’s attributed account of revision and collaboration. Keep language distinction explicit: English with some Hindi. Compress the earlier filmography, plot summary and festival/release chronology; no inferred author fee. Aim for a short reading rather than copying every profile section.

profiles.placement_reason: Keeps the Odisha-connected, cross-language grouping together while preserving the Pratikshya → Anupam → DAMaN making sequence in Part 5. Part 3 is already the longest part, so retain a compact producer-focused reading.
profiles.alternative_considered: Reviewer initially proposed after Anupam in Part 5 to compare production processes; not preferred after considering the uninterrupted recent-film/team momentum.

profiles.name: Pratibha Ray
